tools.name: trust_check
tools.description: Before dealing with an on-chain AI agent: a pass/fail trust verdict with score, tier, badges and the reasoning behind it, for ERC-8004, Olas or Virtuals agents. Each answer states the date its score was computed. Example: id 1380, chain base.

tools.name: reviewer_analysis
tools.description: Who reviewed this agent, and how old are their addresses? Returns the age of every reviewer address and flags patterns such as many addresses created on the same day.

tools.name: compare_agents
tools.description: Side-by-side trust comparison of 2-10 agents, ranked by score with reviewer quality summary for each.

tools.name: address_age
tools.description: Age in days of an address on Base or Ethereum, from its first recorded activity. The answer carries a status: known, no_history (looked up, nothing found on that chain) or unknown (the lookup failed); only known carries a number of days.

tools.name: network_stats
tools.description: Network-wide statistics; total agents by registry, chain distribution, commerce job counts, trust score tier distribution, and every ERC-8004 registration on Ethereum, BNB Chain and Base counted from a daily list.

tools.name: reviewer_wallet
tools.description: Behavior profile for any reviewer wallet; velocity, sweep patterns, score clustering, and sybil signals across the entire ERC-8004 ecosystem. Shows how this wallet behaves when reviewing agents.

tools.name: commerce_stats
tools.description: Paid work history for an agent or address: job count, unique counterparties, repeat client rate, total earnings. Covers Olas Mechs and Virtuals ACP. Give either address, or id together with chain.

tools.name: entity
tools.description: Full operator footprint for any wallet address — all agents owned, trust scores, sybil signals, wallet intelligence, and MCP servers associated with that operator.

tools.name: mcp_attestation
tools.description: ES256-signed attestation for any MCP server. Returns risk score, threat findings, and a signed envelope verifiable against the JWKS endpoint using kid rnwy-mcp-v1.

tools.name: risk_terms
tools.description: Counterparty risk intelligence for any agent. Returns risk tier (low/moderate/elevated/high/severe/critical), raw trust signals, data coverage, and methodology reference. Designed for marketplace operators and escrow providers setting transaction parameters before a deal. Full methodology: https://r

tools.name: leave_note
tools.description: A private note to RNWY: what you were looking for and did not find, a request, a correction, a question. What callers ask for shapes what RNWY builds next. No name, email or key. Stored privately and read by a person at RNWY; never published; a reply is not promised. No IP address is stored with it.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: leave_note · Private data: reviewer_wallet, entity, leave_note · Public sink: leave_note.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: leave_note · Private data: reviewer_wallet, entity, leave_note · Public sink: leave_note

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "trust_check" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

Returns score, tier, badges, and reasoning." → after: "Before dealing with an on-chain AI agent: a pass/fail trust verdict with score, tier, badges and the reasoning behind it, for ERC-8004, Olas or Virtuals agents. findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
